_comment: `preset` is an OBJECT, not the string "conventionalcommits". With the string form, conventional-changelog loads the preset with its own defaults and silently ignores the sibling `types` key — the first attempt at the 0.5.0 changelog contained only Features and Bug Fixes, dropping 9 commits (4 docs, 2 chore, 1 build, 1 refactor, 1 test): exactly the set this preset hides by default. Preset options only take effect nested inside the preset. KNOWN TRADE-OFF: in this form conventional-recommended-bump no longer infers the bump from the commits and falls back to patch, so a release containing a `feat` needs an explicit `npm run release -- --release-as minor`. Verified both ways: object preset + explicit minor gives 0.5.0 with all 7 sections and 35 entries; the string preset gives the right bump and a changelog missing a quarter of the work. A silently incomplete changelog is the worse failure — this repo has been bitten by it before. ALWAYS check the section list and entry count in `--dry-run` before releasing. Separately: `postbump` regenerates dist/tokens.json after package.json is bumped and BEFORE the release commit is made, so the tracked token artifact carries the version it ships with. Without it the release commit touches only CHANGELOG/package.json/lockfile and dist/tokens.json keeps the PREVIOUS version — this repo has published that mismatch before (artifact stamped 0.2.0 while the package was 0.4.1).
